# Issue #7: touching intervals are not merged

`merge_intervals([(1, 3), (3, 5)])` returns `[(1, 3), (3, 5)]` but the documented
behaviour is that closed intervals sharing an endpoint merge into `[(1, 5)]`.
Unsorted input must also be handled. Fix `ranges/merge.py`.

ranges/merge.py
tests/test_merge.py

   3|     Touching intervals, e.g. (1,3) and (3,5), merge into (1,5).
   4|     Input may be unsorted. Returns a sorted list of tuples."""
   5|     if not intervals:
   6|         return []

content: All tests pass and the sanity checks confirm correct behavior: touching intervals merge, unsorted input is handled, overlaps still work, and empty input returns `[]`.

arguments.summary: Fixed `ranges/merge.py`: the merge condition `start < last_end` was changed to `start <= merged[-1][1]` so closed intervals sharing an endpoint (e.g. (1,3) and (3,5)) merge into (1,5), and the input is now sorted before processing so unsorted input is handled correctly. Rewrote the loop to iterate over `sorted(intervals)` and append/merge into an empty `merged` list, avoiding the previous bug where the first element was processed twice. Verified with the existing test suite (2 tests pass) and manual checks for unsorted, overlapping, empty, and point-interval inputs.
